sn35.1:1.1: The “interior” of the title is the “interior” aspect of the sense fields, namely the sensory organs, as opposed to the sense stimuli, which are “exterior” (_bāhira_). This is subtly different from the more common pair _ajjhatta_ and _bahiddha_ (internal/external), which refer to what is inside as opposed to what is outside. For example, the eye of someone else is “interior” (_ajjhattika_) but “external” (_bahiddha_). On the other hand, the touch of one’s own skin is “internal” (_ajjhatta_) but “exterior” (_bāhira_). | Normally in this use we find _ajjhattika_ (literally, “pertaining to the internal”), but _ajjhatta_ is also found, as in the title of this discourse. _Bāhira_, on the other hand, is used consistently in this way. | For context  Chāndogya Upaniṣad 3.12.7 mentions “what is outside a person”.
